thesis: Hellenic Exchanges–Athens Stock Exchange S.A. (ATHEX Group) is Greece's capital markets infrastructure operator. **[Fact]** The Group runs the Athens Stock Exchange, post-trading clearing and settlement (ATHEXCLEAR), and the central securities depository (ATHEXCSD), earning fees on trading, clearing, listings, market data, and technology services without taking directional market risk on customer positions. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated turnover was **€86.3 million** (+58.9% versus €54.3 million in FY2024), EBITDA **€42.2 million**, and net earnings after tax **€31.6 million** (`investor-documents/ir-athex/annual_report_2025.pdf`, Board report). **[Fact]** Weighted average shares were **57,850,000**; earnings per share **€0.622** (`annual_report_2025.pdf`, note 5.39). **[Fact]** In November 2025 Euronext completed a tender offer and holds **74.25%** of voting rights; a new board was constituted in January 2026.
why_market_wrong: FY2025 was an exceptional volume year (+58.9% turnover) ahead of Greece's FTSE Russell upgrade from Advanced Emerging Market to **Developed Market** status effective **21 September 2026**. **[Inference]** Screens and passive models may still treat ATHEX as a small emerging-market venue, while filings show developed-market preparation and Euronext integration already priced into activity. **[Inference]** The market may also capitalize FY2025 peak cash flows; our base case normalizes owner cash below the FY2025 spot of **€0.87** per share from operating activities minus capital spending. **Predictive attribute:** FTSE developed-market reclassification (dated Sept 2026) plus Euronext liquidity cross-listing synergy; partially offset because Euronext already controls the float.
